name: Deep Soft Blue-Violet
lede: Deep Soft Blue-Violet is a muted, darkened reading of [[blue-violet]], from Ridgway's 1912 plates and filed again in the 1955 ISCC-NBS system.

sections.title: Two modifiers at once
sections.body:
The name stacks two modifiers, *deep* and *soft*, on the base color [[blue-violet]]; "soft" in this library grammar marks a lower chroma than the plain name, and "deep" marks a lower lightness [1]. Ridgway's 1912 plate XXIII, hue 55′, tone i, is the recorded source, and the ISCC-NBS system of 1955 later filed the same chip into block 200, named moderate purplish blue in that system's own list [1].

Its closest look-alike is [[greyish-violet-blue]], about 3.4 units off, with its own near-twin [[deep-soft-bluish-violet]] equally close [2]. [[sailor-blue]] and [[gentian-blue]] sit a little further out [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: This match appears in 0.05% of the 23,781 paintings in our archive (12 paintings, as photographed); the within-painting lens narrows that to 3 [3]. In our archive it is rarer than 79% of the named colors [3]. Inside a painting it most often plays a shadow, in 33% of its 3 appearances by lightness rank within the painting [3]. The earliest match dates to 1517, 395 years before the name's 1912 record, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin and a look-alike hue in an aged photograph is not proof of a pigment or dye [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, so the match is a screen comparison, not a pigment identification [3].
